instructionSections.heading: Overview
instructionSections.body: This lesson develops practical competence in professional boundaries and expectations for routine professional cleaning work. Apply the employer’s site procedures and stop if a task falls outside your training or authority.

instructionSections.heading: Instruction
instructionSections.body: Confirm the service agreement, arrival window, access instructions and authorised scope before work. Introduce yourself, obtain consent before entering private areas, and do not photograph personal items without permission.

instructionSections.heading: Prepare and verify
instructionSections.body: Before leaving for the job, read the authorised work order and identify the location, contact, time window, access arrangements, included tasks, exclusions and any special site conditions. If an instruction is unclear, seek confirmation through the designated supervisor or client contact rather than guessing.

instructionSections.heading: Perform the work safely and professionally
instructionSections.body: At arrival, introduce yourself, verify the correct property and explain the planned service. Ask permission before entering private rooms or moving possessions. Keep conversation professional; do not promise additional services, prices or outcomes without authority.

instructionSections.heading: Check, record and escalate
instructionSections.body: If asked to perform an extra task, acknowledge the request, check whether it is in scope, and obtain documented approval before changing the job. Never enter restricted areas or use client equipment without permission.

instructionSections.heading: Learning context and safe boundaries
instructionSections.body: A new cleaner arrives at an occupied home for a two-hour routine clean. The client is working from home and one room is excluded. instructionSections.heading: Step-by-step field procedure
instructionSections.body:
1. Confirm the assignment, address, contact and arrival window from the authorised work order; never assume access or entry permission.
2. On arrival identify yourself, confirm the client or site contact and clarify permitted rooms, pets, alarms and any immediate hazards.
3. Walk the route from entry to storage and exit; locate water, power and waste facilities only where permission is given.
4. Prioritise tasks against the agreed scope and available time; communicate conflicts before changing the service.
5. At closeout check equipment, secure access as instructed and send a factual completion report.

instructionSections.heading: Worked decision and reasoning
instructionSections.body: Worker notices a locked room listed on an old checklist but excluded from today’s order. Do not enter; confirm the current scope with the supervisor. instructionSections.heading: Quality and completion criteria
instructionSections.body: Evidence must show accurate scope interpretation, safe sequencing, correct tool/product selection, respectful communication, and reliable handover. Critical safety failures require stopping the practical and retraining.

instructionSections.heading: Overview

instructionSections.heading: Instruction
instructionSections.body: For injury or exposure, stop work, make the area safe, follow emergency instructions, seek first aid or emergency help as appropriate, and record facts promptly.

instructionSections.heading: Recognise an incident
instructionSections.body: An incident can include injury, near miss, spill, property damage or an unsafe condition. Distinguish immediate danger from an issue that can be safely isolated and reported.

instructionSections.heading: Respond in priority order
instructionSections.body: Stop the affected task, protect yourself and others, and contact emergency services for an emergency using local site procedures. Do not attempt rescue, chemical neutralisation or first aid beyond training.

Determine the required outcome: Cleaning removes visible soil and other contamination; sanitising reduces microorganisms to the level required by the applicable process. Not every kitchen task requires sanitising, and the authorised site plan decides which surfaces and equipment do.

Clean first: Remove food debris and grease with the approved cleaning product and method. Follow label directions for rinsing away detergent residues. A dirty surface can interfere with a sanitiser, so do not skip cleaning unless the site has an expressly validated combined process.

Sanitise according to instructions: Use only a product or process approved for the particular food-contact surface and site. Keep food and clean utensils protected.

Verify and release: Check for visible residue, appropriate completion of contact and rinse requirements, and a safe dry or drain condition as specified. Record the product/process, exceptions and supervisor handover if required. Do not claim sterilisation or microbiological certification from a visual check.

instructionSections.heading: Instruction
instructionSections.body:
Purpose and learning outcome
After this lesson, the learner can demonstrate define acceptance criteria in a routine cleaning workplace, identify limits of their authority and document the result. The following procedures are examples; always apply the approved site process and task instructions.

Detailed workplace method
Read the approved work order line by line. Separate included tasks, exclusions, client preferences, frequency and evidence obligations. Write criteria that an independent inspector can observe: for example, a specified mirror is free of visible streaks under normal room lighting, rather than “looks perfect”. Identify material limitations and pre-existing damage. Do not promise stain removal or restoration outside the agreed scope.

Safety, boundaries and escalation
Before proceeding, confirm the actual work scope, hazards, material or equipment suitability and who can authorise changes. Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside training, or the requested result conflicts with a site instruction. Record facts, not assumptions.

Worked example
A property manager requests a “spotless” kitchen but the work order excludes the inside of the oven. The supervisor records oven interior as excluded, defines checks for benches, sink and appliance exteriors, and asks for written approval before any extra work.

Supervised practical
Give learners a sample scope with ten tasks, two exclusions and three ambiguous phrases. Have them create a checklist with an observable criterion and evidence type for each included task.

Assessment and corrective feedback
An assessor observes the learner and verifies: The checklist matches authorised scope, distinguishes exclusions, contains measurable observations and flags ambiguity before work begins. If any critical safety action is missed, provide coaching and require a new demonstration. Attendance alone is not proof of competence.

instructionSections.heading: Instruction

By the end of this lesson, demonstrate the ability to produce an accurate end-of-shift record while respecting the approved service plan, site procedures and limits of the cleaning role.

lessons.title: Inspection methods and acceptance standards

classification.suggestedLayer: Layer 2 candidate (Group A Cleaning & Hygiene) - Agent 1 to decide

learningOutcomes: Translate scope and client specifications into observable pass/fail criteria

instructionSections.heading: Purpose and scope
instructionSections.body: Inspection methods and acceptance standards is used to verify agreed cleaning outcomes, not to guarantee sterility, restoration or an outcome beyond the signed scope. Read the work order, site instructions, product constraints and client acceptance criteria. Identify what can be observed safely, what requires specialist authorisation, and which uncertainties must be escalated. Translate scope and client specifications into observable pass/fail criteria.

instructionSections.heading: Prepare the inspection
instructionSections.body: Before inspecting, confirm the correct location, work-order version, completion status and any access restrictions. Use a consistent inspection sequence from entrance to exit, top to bottom where appropriate, and clean to dirty. Separate immediate safety hazards from ordinary presentation defects. Choose evidence that is proportionate, lawful and approved by the site. Never disturb hazardous material, open restricted storage or test electrical equipment without authorisation.

instructionSections.heading: Perform and document
instructionSections.body: For each finding record the zone and exact location, the agreed criterion, what was observed, when it was observed, and whether it is a defect, a limitation or a question. Distinguish objective observations from interpretation: “visible residue at basin tap base” is preferable to “poor cleaning”. Photograph only when permitted; avoid faces, personal documents and identifying belongings. Never modify an original record to conceal an error.

instructionSections.heading: Respond and verify
instructionSections.body: Where the finding is within scope, assign a safe corrective action to an authorised worker, agree priority and record completion. Reinspect the same criterion rather than assuming the problem is resolved. Escalate damage, exposure risks, disputes and work outside the contract. If a product or procedure requires specialist testing, record that testing was not performed; do not invent a result.

instructionSections.heading: Worked workplace example
instructionSections.body: A customer calls a surface dirty although the agreed scope excludes restoration; distinguish service defect from scope variation. A sound response identifies the agreed standard, makes a factual observation, records the limitation, requests approval when required, and communicates the outcome without assigning blame.

instructionSections.heading: Guided practical
instructionSections.body: Compare three cleaned zones against a signed scope and record objective findings. The learner must explain each choice, identify at least one privacy or safety constraint, record a finding with a timestamp and location, and show how a supervisor would verify any correction.

instructionSections.heading: Common mistakes and corrections
instructionSections.body: Avoid treating a photograph as proof of disinfection, confusing a pre-existing defect with a missed task, recording personal information unnecessarily, or closing a finding without reinspection. Correct these by using a scope-linked checklist, objective descriptions, minimum-necessary evidence and a documented closeout step.

instructionSections.heading: Knowledge and transfer
instructionSections.body: Explain why the agreed acceptance criterion must be identified before judging a surface. Describe how to record an observation that a different inspector can independently verify. State when inspection must stop and be escalated. Apply the same process to a new site with different privacy and access requirements.

instructionSections.heading: Instruction
instructionSections.body:
Learning outcome
By the end of this lesson, demonstrate the ability to obtain consent and preserve dignity while respecting the approved service plan, site procedures and limits of the cleaning role.

Workplace procedure
Introduce yourself and explain the cleaning task in plain language. Confirm the person is comfortable with your presence and the work area; respect refusals and requests for privacy. Follow the authorised service plan and your role boundaries. Do not provide personal care, handle medication, make financial decisions or move mobility aids without permission and training. If consent is unclear or the person appears distressed, pause the task and contact the designated coordinator.

Decision boundaries
Before acting, confirm authorisation, hazards and the person responsible for escalation. If the task exceeds training, consent, safe access or agreed scope, pause the affected work, protect others as appropriate, report promptly and document the reason. Never substitute an improvised method for a required specialist procedure.

Worked workplace example
A client asks the cleaner to help with medication. The cleaner politely explains that this is outside the cleaning role and contacts the care coordinator through the agreed process.

Guided practical exercise
Role-play a first visit where the client declines bedroom access and requests an out-of-scope personal task. Demonstrate respectful language and documentation.

Assessment and feedback
An assessor should observe a complete demonstration and confirm: Seeks meaningful consent, respects refusal and maintains the professional scope without coercion. If a critical safety, privacy or consent step is missed, provide targeted feedback and require reassessment before signoff.
